title: Canonical glueing object of one module
statement: Let R and S be commutative rings, φ : R → S a ring homomorphism, t a natural number, and f : Fin t → R. For every R-module M, there is an object X of the formal glueing category [def-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-data] with prime module S tensor_R M, chart i the canonical R_(f i)-module M_(f i), comparison maps compare φ (f i) M and overlap maps swap (f i) (f j) M. The bundled module equalities are literal equalities and the map identifications are heterogeneous equalities. This assertion constructs one object only, not a functor or morphism assignment.

proof.text: Take the prescribed scalar extension and localized chart modules. Prove the literal equality of each restricted chart with the localized R-module by Module.ext' and algebraMap_smul. Use compare_properties for comparison bijectivity, compare_smul for S-linearity, and the inverse identities in swap_properties for swap bijectivity. Transport these equivalences along the chart equalities, retaining heterogeneous equalities of their linear maps.

Every denominator acts bijectively on the target of the square and cocycle: outer localization inverts its denominator, localization preserves scalar bijectivity, and scalar extension preserves it by tensoring a linear equivalence. Apply localization uniqueness twice to the square and three times to the cocycle. On images of pure tensors the square follows from the denominator-one formulas of exists_compare, localMap and exists_swap, with additivity extending to arbitrary tensors. On the original module the cocycle follows from the same denominator-one swap and localized-map formulas. Transport the two equations along the chart equalities and the heterogeneous linear-map identifications to fill Data.square and Data.cocycle.

proof_origin.place: Remark 05EL, https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05EL; S3 Lean proof by localization uniqueness, 2026-10-13

mathlib_searches.results: CategoryTheory.Functor.of and Functorial package an already supplied morphism assignment and laws; no canonical formal glueing construction.
Functor, Functor.obj, Functor.map, identity and composition constructors. These do not establish the glueing object or morphism compatibility identities.

Mathlib has sheaf/topological glueing, not this formal glueing construction. Sheaf.Paper.FormalGlueingCanonicalMaps supplies fraction formulas, bijectivity and localized map laws. FormalGlueingData supplies the category and definitions. LinearMap.baseChange_id and baseChange_comp are in Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.TensorProduct.Tower. No duplicate of either intermediate theorem in lean/Sheaf or lean/WeilConjectures.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_canonical_functor_objects {R : Type u} {S : Type v}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (φ : R →+* S) (t : ℕ) (f : Fin t → R)
    (M : ModuleCat.{max u v w} R) :
    ∃ X : Data.{u, v, max u v w} φ f,
      X.M' = extend φ M ∧
      (∀ i : Fin t, X.M i =
        ModuleCat.of (Localization.Away (f i)) (LocalizedModule.Away (f i) M)) ∧
      (∀ i : Fin t, HEq (X.alpha i).toLinearMap (compare φ (f i) M)) ∧
      (∀ i j : Fin t, HEq (X.alpha_overlap i j).toLinearMap (swap (f i) (f j) M))
